constraints: All proposed times use the Europe/Lisbon timezone offset in effect for 11–15 January 2027, which is +00:00.
The Advanced Physics Final Exam on Wednesday 13 January from 16:00 to 18:00 is fixed and already present in the calendar, so it is not moved or recreated.
The protected 8-hour sleep blocks are left unchanged every night.

The Wednesday 16:00 commute to the High-Performance Center and the Wednesday 16:30 technical training are fixed/protected items, but exact externally confirmed delete exceptions were supplied for both, so deleting them is operationally permitted.
The requested 30-minute transit after the exam is added from 18:00 to 18:30.

The calendar already contains 6.5 hours of Physics study before the exam: Monday 14:00–16:00, Tuesday 10:00–12:30, and Wednesday 10:30–12:30. This satisfies the requested minimum of 6 hours without moving study blocks.
The Wednesday evening make-up session uses the coach-offered 19:00–20:30 option, but the exact venue, coach supervision, and equipment availability still need confirmation with the coach.
Deleting the Wednesday coffee social affects peers, so it should be confirmed with friends or the study group.
priorities: Protect the official exam and keep the calendar clear during the exam window.
Preserve sleep exactly as scheduled because sleep has the highest protection level.
Maintain the training load by replacing the missed Wednesday afternoon technical session with the coach-offered Wednesday evening individual make-up session.
Avoid moving or deleting unrelated fixed/protected events without an exact supplied exception.
Prefer the Wednesday make-up over Friday conditioning because it directly replaces the missed technical session and does not require disturbing Friday’s fixed commute/training structure.

alternatives_considered.option: Use the Friday 14:00–15:30 extra conditioning block instead of Wednesday evening make-up training.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Friday 14:00–15:30 is free on the calendar, but the location and travel logistics are not confirmed. If it is at the High-Performance Center, it creates uncertainty with the existing fixed Friday 16:00 commute to the High-Performance Center, which cannot be moved or deleted without an exception. It is also a conditioning block rather than a direct technical make-up.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the Wednesday coffee social unchanged.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It overlaps the proposed Wednesday 19:00–20:30 make-up training from 19:30 to 20:30. The make-up training is higher priority because it replaces a training session missed due to the mandatory exam.

alternatives_considered.option: Move the Wednesday coffee social later on Wednesday evening.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A later 90-minute social would run too close to or into the protected 22:30 sleep start once travel uncertainty is considered. The friends’ availability is also unknown.

alternatives_considered.option: Move the original Wednesday afternoon training instead of deleting it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The only externally confirmed exception for the protected Wednesday training is deletion, not a move. The make-up training is therefore added as a new coach-offered session rather than moving the protected original event.

rationale.summary: The plan keeps the mandatory Physics exam and all protected sleep intact, removes the conflicting Wednesday commute and technical training using the supplied exact exceptions, adds the required 30-minute post-exam transit buffer, and schedules the coach-offered Wednesday 19:00–20:30 individual make-up training. The existing Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday morning Physics study blocks already provide 6.5 hours before the exam, so no extra study changes are needed. Confirm the Wednesday evening make-up details with the coach, and confirm cancellation of the Wednesday coffee social with friends.

weaknesses: The plan places Make-up Individual Technical Training on Wednesday 19:00–20:30 immediately after a 16:00–18:00 Advanced Physics Final Exam and a 18:00–18:30 post-exam transit buffer, but the rationale does not meaningfully assess the combined cognitive and physical load of exam day.

Wednesday has no explicit dinner or substantial recovery block between the 18:00 exam finish and 19:00 training start. There is only 18:30–19:00 unallocated time before training, and the next protected sleep block starts at 22:30. This may still be workable, but the proposal treats the slot mainly as available rather than explaining how basic post-exam food, decompression, preparation, and training readiness are handled.

The Wednesday evening make-up depends on coach-offered details that the rationale itself says still need confirmation: venue, coach supervision, and equipment availability. That is not a technical violation, but it is central to whether the added 19:00–20:30 session is actually usable.

The alternative analysis compares Wednesday make-up against Friday conditioning mostly on technical/training-type grounds, but it does not clearly weigh whether avoiding an exam-evening training session could be more sustainable despite being a less direct replacement.

The final calendar’s added events have null category, importance, fixed status, participants, and descriptions despite the proposal describing them as commute/training with importance and user participation. The metadata note says this is contractual rather than a new preference, so it is not necessarily invalid, but it weakens the human-readable evidence for how the added commitments should be treated.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The resulting calendar is technically coherent and protects the fixed exam and sleep blocks, but the proposed organization creates a materially demanding Wednesday: recovery/mobility 07:00–08:30, physiotherapy 09:00–10:00, Physics study 10:30–12:30, exam 16:00–18:00, post-exam transit 18:00–18:30, and make-up technical training 19:00–20:30. The rationale is clear about operational permissions and priorities, yet it under-explains whether training one hour after a final exam is realistically sustainable, especially with only a short visible gap before training and no explicit dinner on Wednesday. A revision should not automatically abandon the same operations, but should either substantiate why this exam-evening make-up is manageable in the fuller context or reconsider whether a less compressed distribution could preserve the visible priorities with less dependence on post-exam stamina and unconfirmed logistics. Request satisfaction cannot be independently verified because the original request is not provided and technical validation explicitly did not check request satisfaction or soft preferences.

This is not an objective incompatibility, and the preserved 22:30–06:30 sleep block helps, but the practical manageability of the added session is under-substantiated.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Reconsider the distribution using the fuller context: either justify why the Wednesday evening make-up is realistic after the exam, including how post-exam food, preparation, recovery, venue, and coach logistics are handled, or compare it more directly with less compressed options that may reduce exam-day load while still respecting the visible priorities and protected events.

changes.title: Post-exam food and training preparation buffer

constraints: All proposed times use the Europe/Lisbon timezone offset in effect for 11–15 January 2027, which is +00:00.
The Advanced Physics Final Exam on Wednesday 13 January from 16:00 to 18:00 is fixed and already present in the calendar, so it is not moved or recreated.
The protected 8-hour sleep blocks are left unchanged every night, including Wednesday night 22:30–06:30 after the exam-day changes.

The Wednesday 16:00 commute to the High-Performance Center and the Wednesday 16:30 technical training are fixed/protected items, but exact externally confirmed delete exceptions were supplied for both, so deleting them is operationally permitted.
The requested 30-minute transit after the exam is reserved from 18:00 to 18:30.

The calendar already contains 6.5 hours of Physics study before the exam: Monday 14:00–16:00, Tuesday 10:00–12:30, and Wednesday 10:30–12:30. This satisfies the requested minimum of at least 6 hours across Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday morning without moving existing study blocks.

The Wednesday evening make-up training uses one of the two coach-offered options, 19:00–20:30, but its venue, equipment, exact supervision arrangement, and whether the post-exam transit ends at the correct location still need confirmation with the coach.

A 30-minute post-exam food and preparation buffer is reserved between transit and training, and a 60-minute post-training dinner and recovery block is reserved before the protected sleep block. These are calendar reservations for basic needs; the exact food, recovery routine, and training readiness are personal-context unknowns and are not assumed.
Deleting the Wednesday coffee social affects peers, so that cancellation should be confirmed with the study group or friends.
priorities: Protect the official exam and keep the calendar clear during the exam window.
Protect all sleep blocks because sleep is a hard constraint and has the highest performance priority.
Preserve the required Physics study target using existing study time rather than adding unnecessary academic load.
Replace the missed Wednesday technical session with the closest direct coach-offered make-up option, while explicitly reserving time for transit, food, preparation, dinner, and recovery.
Avoid moving or deleting unrelated fixed events without an exact supplied exception.

Prefer the Wednesday individual technical make-up over the Friday conditioning option because it is a direct substitute for the missed technical session and avoids creating an additional Friday double-training afternoon with uncertain venue and commute implications.

alternatives_considered.option: Use the Friday 14:00–15:30 extra conditioning block instead of Wednesday evening make-up training.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This would reduce the immediate exam-evening load, but it is a conditioning block rather than a direct technical replacement. It also creates a demanding Friday sequence before the fixed 16:00 commute and 16:30–18:30 pre-weekend scrimmage. The venue is unknown: if the conditioning block is at the High-Performance Center, it may require a pre-14:00 commute or adjustment to the existing fixed 16:00 commute, neither of which is externally confirmed. If it is elsewhere, the transition into the fixed Friday training structure still needs coach confirmation.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the Wednesday coffee social unchanged.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It overlaps the proposed Wednesday 19:00–20:30 make-up training from 19:30 to 20:30. The make-up training has higher priority because it replaces a protected training session missed due to the mandatory exam.

alternatives_considered.option: Move the Wednesday coffee social later on Wednesday evening.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: After training ends at 20:30, the schedule needs dinner and recovery before the protected 22:30 sleep block. A later 90-minute social would compress recovery and sleep preparation, and friends’ availability is unknown.

alternatives_considered.option: Move the original Wednesday afternoon training instead of deleting it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The only externally confirmed exception for the protected Wednesday training is deletion, not a move. The make-up training is therefore added as a new coach-offered session rather than moving the protected original event.

alternatives_considered.option: Add more Physics study before the exam.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The existing Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday morning Physics study blocks already provide 6.5 hours before the exam, satisfying the user’s minimum. Adding more study would increase exam-week fatigue without being required by the stated target.

rationale.summary: The revised plan keeps the same core exam and training solution but makes the exam-day feasibility more explicit. It deletes only the two protected Wednesday items covered by exact external exceptions, keeps all sleep unchanged, preserves the already sufficient 6.5 hours of Physics study, adds the required 18:00–18:30 post-exam transit buffer, reserves 18:30–19:00 for food and training preparation, schedules the coach-offered 19:00–20:30 individual technical make-up, and reserves 20:30–21:30 for dinner and recovery before the 22:30 sleep block. This is still a demanding Wednesday after a final exam, so the make-up should be confirmed with the coach for venue, equipment, supervision, and realistic readiness; the Wednesday coffee cancellation should be confirmed with friends. The Friday conditioning alternative is less compressed after the exam, but it introduces a different fatigue risk and more uncertainty around venue and commute before the already fixed Friday afternoon training.

Another revision is not clearly required from the visible information alone, because the main remaining risks are explicitly identified as conditions to verify rather than contradictions in the proposed organization. plausibility_review.reason: The main human-quality risk is the placement of a high-priority individual technical training session on Wednesday 19:00–20:30 after a 16:00–18:00 final exam, with only a 18:00–18:30 transit buffer and 30 additional minutes before training. Given the visible week already includes repeated early commutes, morning training, academic blocks, and afternoon/evening training, the proposal should more directly address fatigue, food, preparation, and recovery on exam day. This is not an objective incompatibility, and the preserved 22:30–06:30 sleep block helps, but the practical manageability of the added session is under-substantiated.
plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: Reconsider the distribution using the fuller context: either justify why the Wednesday evening make-up is realistic after the exam, including how post-exam food, preparation, recovery, venue, and coach logistics are handled, or compare it more directly with less compressed options that may reduce exam-day load while still respecting the visible priorities and protected events.

unresolved_assumptions.assumption: The user can sustain the week’s combined athletic and academic load, including morning training on Monday through Friday, multiple afternoon training sessions, Physics exam preparation, the Wednesday final exam, and the added Wednesday evening make-up session.
unresolved_assumptions.evidence_gap: The rationale preserves sleep and existing commitments but does not assess cumulative fatigue or whether adding training after the exam is appropriate for the user’s recovery needs.

unresolved_assumptions.subject: Coffee social cancellation

unresolved_assumptions.evidence_gap: The rationale notes that cancellation affects peers and should be confirmed, but no confirmation is present in the structured proposal.

weaknesses: The plan places Make-up Individual Technical Training on Wednesday 19:00–20:30 immediately after a 16:00–18:00 Advanced Physics Final Exam and a 18:00–18:30 post-exam transit buffer, but the rationale does not meaningfully assess the combined cognitive and physical load of exam day.

Wednesday has no explicit dinner or substantial recovery block between the 18:00 exam finish and 19:00 training start. There is only 18:30–19:00 unallocated time before training, and the next protected sleep block starts at 22:30. This may still be workable, but the proposal treats the slot mainly as available rather than explaining how basic post-exam food, decompression, preparation, and training readiness are handled.

The Wednesday evening make-up depends on coach-offered details that the rationale itself says still need confirmation: venue, coach supervision, and equipment availability. That is not a technical violation, but it is central to whether the added 19:00–20:30 session is actually usable.

The alternative analysis compares Wednesday make-up against Friday conditioning mostly on technical/training-type grounds, but it does not clearly weigh whether avoiding an exam-evening training session could be more sustainable despite being a less direct replacement.

The final calendar’s added events have null category, importance, fixed status, participants, and descriptions despite the proposal describing them as commute/training with importance and user participation. The metadata note says this is contractual rather than a new preference, so it is not necessarily invalid, but it weakens the human-readable evidence for how the added commitments should be treated.
prior_critic_reviews.feedback: The resulting calendar is technically coherent and protects the fixed exam and sleep blocks, but the proposed organization creates a materially demanding Wednesday: recovery/mobility 07:00–08:30, physiotherapy 09:00–10:00, Physics study 10:30–12:30, exam 16:00–18:00, post-exam transit 18:00–18:30, and make-up technical training 19:00–20:30. The rationale is clear about operational permissions and priorities, yet it under-explains whether training one hour after a final exam is realistically sustainable, especially with only a short visible gap before training and no explicit dinner on Wednesday. A revision should not automatically abandon the same operations, but should either substantiate why this exam-evening make-up is manageable in the fuller context or reconsider whether a less compressed distribution could preserve the visible priorities with less dependence on post-exam stamina and unconfirmed logistics. Request satisfaction cannot be independently verified because the original request is not provided and technical validation explicitly did not check request satisfaction or soft preferences.

changes.title: Post-exam food and training preparation buffer

constraints: All proposed times use the Europe/Lisbon timezone offset in effect for 11–15 January 2027, which is +00:00.
The Advanced Physics Final Exam on Wednesday 13 January from 16:00 to 18:00 is fixed and already present in the calendar, so it is not moved or recreated.
The protected 8-hour sleep blocks are left unchanged every night, including Wednesday night 22:30–06:30 after the exam-day changes.

The Wednesday 16:00 commute to the High-Performance Center and the Wednesday 16:30 technical training are fixed/protected items, but exact externally confirmed delete exceptions were supplied for both, so deleting them is operationally permitted.
The requested 30-minute transit after the exam is reserved from 18:00 to 18:30.

The calendar already contains 6.5 hours of Physics study before the exam: Monday 14:00–16:00, Tuesday 10:00–12:30, and Wednesday 10:30–12:30. This satisfies the requested minimum of at least 6 hours across Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday morning without moving existing study blocks.

The Wednesday evening make-up training uses one of the two coach-offered options, 19:00–20:30, but its venue, equipment, exact supervision arrangement, and whether the post-exam transit ends at the correct location still need confirmation with the coach.

A 30-minute post-exam food and preparation buffer is reserved between transit and training, and a 60-minute post-training dinner and recovery block is reserved before the protected sleep block. These are calendar reservations for basic needs; the exact food, recovery routine, and training readiness are personal-context unknowns and are not assumed.
Deleting the Wednesday coffee social affects peers, so that cancellation should be confirmed with the study group or friends.
priorities: Protect the official exam and keep the calendar clear during the exam window.
Protect all sleep blocks because sleep is a hard constraint and has the highest performance priority.
Preserve the required Physics study target using existing study time rather than adding unnecessary academic load.
Replace the missed Wednesday technical session with the closest direct coach-offered make-up option, while explicitly reserving time for transit, food, preparation, dinner, and recovery.
Avoid moving or deleting unrelated fixed events without an exact supplied exception.

Prefer the Wednesday individual technical make-up over the Friday conditioning option because it is a direct substitute for the missed technical session and avoids creating an additional Friday double-training afternoon with uncertain venue and commute implications.

alternatives_considered.option: Use the Friday 14:00–15:30 extra conditioning block instead of Wednesday evening make-up training.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This would reduce the immediate exam-evening load, but it is a conditioning block rather than a direct technical replacement. It also creates a demanding Friday sequence before the fixed 16:00 commute and 16:30–18:30 pre-weekend scrimmage. The venue is unknown: if the conditioning block is at the High-Performance Center, it may require a pre-14:00 commute or adjustment to the existing fixed 16:00 commute, neither of which is externally confirmed. If it is elsewhere, the transition into the fixed Friday training structure still needs coach confirmation.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the Wednesday coffee social unchanged.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It overlaps the proposed Wednesday 19:00–20:30 make-up training from 19:30 to 20:30. The make-up training has higher priority because it replaces a protected training session missed due to the mandatory exam.

alternatives_considered.option: Move the Wednesday coffee social later on Wednesday evening.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: After training ends at 20:30, the schedule needs dinner and recovery before the protected 22:30 sleep block. A later 90-minute social would compress recovery and sleep preparation, and friends’ availability is unknown.

alternatives_considered.option: Move the original Wednesday afternoon training instead of deleting it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The only externally confirmed exception for the protected Wednesday training is deletion, not a move. The make-up training is therefore added as a new coach-offered session rather than moving the protected original event.

alternatives_considered.option: Add more Physics study before the exam.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The existing Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday morning Physics study blocks already provide 6.5 hours before the exam, satisfying the user’s minimum. Adding more study would increase exam-week fatigue without being required by the stated target.

rationale.summary: The revised plan keeps the same core exam and training solution but makes the exam-day feasibility more explicit. It deletes only the two protected Wednesday items covered by exact external exceptions, keeps all sleep unchanged, preserves the already sufficient 6.5 hours of Physics study, adds the required 18:00–18:30 post-exam transit buffer, reserves 18:30–19:00 for food and training preparation, schedules the coach-offered 19:00–20:30 individual technical make-up, and reserves 20:30–21:30 for dinner and recovery before the 22:30 sleep block. This is still a demanding Wednesday after a final exam, so the make-up should be confirmed with the coach for venue, equipment, supervision, and realistic readiness; the Wednesday coffee cancellation should be confirmed with friends. The Friday conditioning alternative is less compressed after the exam, but it introduces a different fatigue risk and more uncertainty around venue and commute before the already fixed Friday afternoon training.
